result:
result: Borrow 2 items, adapt 5, skip 2 (of 9 tstack skills); none needs a new skill file, and all land as edits to existing root text.

All tstack facts come from reading the 16 files in the clone at `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-holyagent/e4ac10e5-b710-572b-aa70-34045c8c8d11/scratchpad/ext/tstack`; nothing was executed. Every skill path below is relative to that root. I did not check the repo's git history.

**tstack skills (sourced)**
- `skills/full-send/SKILL.md` (plus `agents/openai.yaml`): the user says "full send", and the agent goes from change to proof, review, PR, babysit and merge without asking. It grants merge and `--force-with-lease` on the PR's own branch. It also waives ask-first test rules and defines a "merge gate" (see the first list below).
- `skills/full-stop/SKILL.md`: the full-send flow, but it never merges. It disables auto-merge first and hands off at the merge gate.
- `skills/council/SKILL.md`: three delegates from three providers review the work. Each gives a score out of 10, rounds repeat until they are satisfied, and a score table goes into the PR description.
- `skills/sol-loop/SKILL.md`: a single GPT Sol reviewer in a loop. It has a 3-round budget (5 for security-sensitive work), a finding ledger, and severities blocker/should/nit. It tells the agent to make the smallest fix and to push back on scope creep.
- `skills/file-pr/SKILL.md`: a PR that leads with the problem rather than an inventory of changes. It checks for an existing PR, follows the repo's title conventions, scans for secrets, and ends with a "Created with <model> in <harness>" line. It falls back to the REST API when the GraphQL limit is used up.
- `skills/babysit-pr/SKILL.md` and `skills/babysit-pr/scripts/pr-wait`: one watcher per PR, no hand-written polling. Findings are verified before acting. CodeRabbit is advisory, and PR growth is capped by declining marginal fixes. It never merges unless the user asked, and checks for BEHIND/DIRTY and overlapping base commits before merging.
- `skills/modernize/SKILL.md`: rebase an old PR, then choose MODERNIZE, REWORK or CLOSE by checking whether the idea still belongs. It uses `git range-diff` and `--force-with-lease` against the head SHA observed before the rebase.
- `skills/takeover/SKILL.md`: finish someone else's PR, branch or thread. It keeps Git authorship and co-author credit, imports their commits onto a new branch, and does not trust the handoff.
- `skills/leaving-pr-comments/SKILL.md`: every agent comment is prefixed with a `> [!NOTE] 🤖 **<model> responding on behalf of <user>**` callout, followed by a direct, concise style.

**Detail in full-send and pr-wait (sourced)**
- The full-send merge gate has five conditions on the latest head: proof covers the whole diff, required checks are green, bot findings are fixed or dismissed with a written reason, no human review requests changes, and the branch is current and mergeable.
- `pr-wait` is a 557-line Python script. It polls GraphQL and `gh` every 20 seconds and keeps a per-PR lock and state under `~/.local/state/pr-wait`.
- `pr-wait` pre-reads the required checks from branch protection, so a required check that has not started counts as pending.
- It requires two identical polls in a row before calling checks finished.
- It reports when the base branch moves and touches files in the PR.
- It prints one line per event and exits 0 or 1 depending on whether the PR needs the agent.

**holyagent counterparts (sourced)**
- `packages/runtime/src/instructions/claude-5.5/root/ci.md`: CI watched with Monitor running `gh pr checks <n> --watch`, aggregated Failed, then Unknown, then Pending, then Passed, per head SHA.
- `root/version-control.md` and `root/stack-plan.md`: never force-push or rewrite published history, merge forward instead, and only the root commits.
- `requirements/commit-text.md`: no agent or Co-Authored-By text in commits or PRs.
- `root/pr-text.md`: a one-line rule about what changed, why, how it was checked and what remains.
- `root/asking.md` and `skills/user-busy/SKILL.md`: unattended-mode rules (see below).
- `requirements/mergeability.md`: the six merge-readiness dimensions.

**Recommendations**

Items with a "Reason" line are my inference, in the same sense as the opening paragraph's summary.

| tstack skill | Class | Lands in | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| `babysit-pr` (concepts only) | Adapt | `root/ci.md` | Add four rules to the CI text: read required checks up front so unstarted ones count as Pending, require a stable snapshot before declaring checks finished, flag base commits that touch the PR's files, and let CodeRabbit-style bots be advisory. |
| `pr-wait` (the script) | Skip | none | It is Python, hand-polls, and keeps external state. That conflicts with Effect/Bun and with `gh pr checks --watch` plus Monitor, which `root/ci.md` already uses. |
| `modernize` | Adapt | New short section in `root/stack-plan.md` (or a `reviewer-audit` check) | Borrow the MODERNIZE/REWORK/CLOSE verdict and the "check whether the idea is still wanted" step. Drop `--force-with-lease`, because holyagent forbids rewriting published history; use merge-forward. |
| `file-pr` | Adapt | `root/pr-text.md` | Borrow "lead with the problem, not an inventory", a check for an existing PR, a secrets scan before submit, and the REST fallback. Skip the model/harness footer, because commit-text.md bans agent attribution. |
| `takeover` | Adapt | `root/version-control.md` plus a short Assignment pattern | Borrow "treat the handoff as context, not proof", keeping human authorship and co-author credit, and recording what was inherited. Drop the model-attribution part. |
| `sol-loop` (practice only) | Adapt | Review stage guidance in `root/assignments.md` or `roles/reviewer-code/purpose.md` | Borrow the round budget, the finding ledger, severity demotion for rare cases, "smallest fix", and "do not agree just to end the loop". Skip the Sol-specific delegation. |
| `full-send` | Adapt | `root/asking.md` / `skills/user-busy/SKILL.md` | Borrow the explicit merge gate as a checklist, and "stay active until the end". Skip the grants to merge, force-push, and waive ask-first test rules, which conflict with `version-control.md`, `merge-ready.md` and "merge needs the user's approval". |
| `full-stop` | Borrow | `root/ci.md` or `user-busy` | It already matches holyagent's rule that the root hands off and merging needs approval. The extra worth taking is to disable auto-merge and check the PR is open and not a draft before handoff. |
| `leaving-pr-comments` | Borrow (partial) | `root/ci.md`, the line about replying on a thread | Borrow the style rules: lead with the conclusion, cite evidence, separate fact from judgment, preview before posting, and resolve a thread only after posting. Skip the robot/model callout, which conflicts with commit-text.md. |
| `council` | Skip | none | It needs three providers, and the Claude plugin has one. The existing `reviewer-*` specialists cover multi-angle review. Only the "no invented scores" idea is worth keeping, and `sol-loop`'s ledger covers it. |

**Top 3 priorities**
1. `babysit-pr` concepts into `root/ci.md`: small and concrete, and it improves CI accuracy without breaking any rule.
2. `sol-loop` budget and ledger practices into the review guidance: they cut scope creep across review rounds.
3. `modernize` verdicts and `file-pr` problem-first PR text, into `stack-plan.md` and `pr-text.md`.

**Inference and limits**
- Sourced above: the tstack contents and the holyagent files I read.
- Inference: every classification and "Reason" is my judgment, not stated in either repo.
- Not read: the specialist `conduct.md`/`merge-ready.md` details beyond the grep hits, `docs/*.md` and `lefthook.yml`. I did not confirm whether holyagent already has a review-round limit; the grep found only a passing mention.
- Versions: tstack was read as cloned today, with no version tag. The clone is shallow.
